subject: AcreetionOS Update — July 24, 2026
body:
The AcreetionOS continuous integration pipeline has been further refined with the implementation of per-pipeline staging directories, significantly reducing the likelihood of publish races between concurrent builds and making our ISO build process more efficient. This improvement is a testament to the community's dedication to refining and stabilizing our workflow, ensuring that users receive the most up-to-date and stable versions of AcreetionOS.

Development
The latest updates to our CI pipeline are a result of the community's efforts to streamline and improve the development process, with the added benefit of relative symlinks for the latest.iso file, making it easier to access and manage our ISO builds. For more information on our development process and how to get involved, visit our website at https://acreetionos.org/ and explore our documentation at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html.

Community
The release of Emacs 31.1 has generated excitement within the community, with its numerous changes and improvements, and we're eager to see how it will be utilized within the AcreetionOS ecosystem. Additionally, the community has been actively engaged in discussing and implementing security updates, such as those issued on Monday, and exploring the latest stable kernel sets, including the 7.1.10 and 6.18.46 releases, which can be found in our changelog at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html. For more information on our community and how to participate, visit our wiki at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html. 

Tip of the day
To stay up-to-date with the latest developments and security updates, be sure to check our flash page at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html regularly, where you can find the latest news and information on AcreetionOS.
